problem: Joint actions and native proprioception entangle task interaction with the morphology of the source embodiment.
contribution: KITE separates an embodiment-agnostic interaction policy from kinematics-trained embodiment-specific decoders using a latent contact-intent interface.
algorithm: Encode sparse world-frame surface contact locations/normals into a permutation-invariant latent intent. Jointly learn intent encoding and decoder bank from synthetic kinematic examples; freeze them and train a source-task imitation policy predicting latent intents from observations and previous intent.
observations: Task observations plus previous latent intent rather than source-native joint state; target decoders additionally condition on target configuration.
actions: Shared latent intent, decoded into target goal joint configuration; target kinematics are available during pretraining even when target-task demonstrations are absent.
embodiment_and_data: Parallel gripper, dexterous hands and composite tool embodiments; object placing, keyboard pressing, bottle pumping and nut rotating. Simulation demonstrations include2400grasping/scripted objectplacing trajectories and800for several other tasks.
experiments: Cross-embodiment transfer, adding a new decoder, target-demonstration ablation and initial-pose perturbations; realWuji transfer uses10trials per task. Nut rotation's reported percentage is a normalized rotation ratio, not a binary episode fraction.
baselines: Joint/retargeting and policy alternatives plus OracleIntent/decoder diagnostics; compare target-task demonstration additions separately from access to target kinematics.

quantitative_result.decoder_diagnostic: OracleIntent placing falls from85%base to57%after30cm shift
quantitative_result.scope: Source paper's specified embodiments, not SO101-to-ROSMASTER validation.

limitations: Decoder training is local around perturbed configurations and does not ensure arbitrary initialization or reachable intent. Contact extraction depends on object/surface geometry. The authorpage says code forthcoming; no installable implementation was verified.
hardware_adaptation: Treat as a close conceptual competitor. An initial Explorer object-relative FK/IK baseline is not KITE replication; learned intent/decoders require accurate meshes, contact models, synthetic data and separate target validation.
algorithm_detail: The intent interface carries sparsecontact points and normals with variablecardinality, compressed by a setencoder. Contact-relevant joint masks prevent synthetic targets from imposing arbitrary changes on uninvolved joints. Source trajectories are transformed throughFK to persistent selected surface points, including approach frames.
integration_contract: Version mesh/kinematic and object registration inputs, surface-contact selection, latent encoder and every targetdecoder together. Explicitly label target-kinematics access and absence/presence of task demonstrations. Reject unreachable or out-of-domain initializations.
license_evidence: PrimaryarXivPDF and authorpage were inspected; authorpage exposes Code soon, so there is no verified code/model license or execution evidence. An independent baseline cannot be labeled upstream reuse.
required_experiments: Kinematic synthesis sanitychecks; decoder heldoutpose tests; contact/geometric uncertainty; matched target-only and FK/IK baselines; smallN intervals; separate binarysuccess versus rotation-ratio metrics; supervised hardwarevalidation only after safety admission.
difference_from_explorer: The contactintent/kinematicdecoder split is already published. Explorer must isolate a different tested mechanism in evidence management, transfer/adaptation, retention or diagnosis instead of claiming this split as new.
